description: Ensemble weather forecast products from NOAA's RRFS Ensemble Forecast System (REFS).

links.title: NOAA RRFS and REFS on NOAA Open Data Dissemination

attribution: NOAA NWS NCEP REFS data processed by dynamical.org from NOAA Open Data Dissemination archives.
description_summary:
This dataset is an archive of past and present REFS ensemble products, optimized for spatial (map) access patterns. Forecasts are identified by an initialization time (`init_time`) denoting the start time of the model run, and step forward hourly along the `lead_time` dimension from 1 hour out to 60 hours.

Ensemble means and standard deviations are stored along the `statistic` dimension. Other products, such as probabilities of exceeding a threshold, are separate variables.

This dataset uses the native RRFS Lambert Conformal Conic projection, with spatial indexing along the `x` and `y` dimensions. The example notebook shows how to use the embedded spatial reference to select geographic areas of interest.

Note: `dynamical-catalog>=1.0.1` and `gribberish>=1.8.4` (or `zarr>=3.2 icechunk>=2.0 gribberish>=1.8.4`) are required.
description_details:
### Source

The source grib files this archive is constructed from are provided by [NOAA Open Data Dissemination (NODD)](https://www.noaa.gov/information-technology/open-data-dissemination) and accessed from the [AWS Open Data Registry](https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-rrfs-ops/).

### Storage

Storage for this dataset is generously provided by [AWS Open Data](https://aws.amazon.com/opendata/).

### Chunks

This dataset is stored in [Zarr](https://zarr.dev/) format, which splits each variable into a grid of **chunks** — the smallest unit read from storage. When possible, aligning your reads with this dataset's chunk grid can significantly improve data access speed.

The element count and coordinate span of this dataset:

| dimension | chunk |
|---|---|
| init_time | 1 (6 hours) |
| statistic | 1 |
| lead_time | 1 (1 hour) |
| y | 1059 (3177 km) |
| x | 1799 (5397 km) |
| **uncompressed** | 14.5 MiB |

### Validation report

Review the [validation report](https://dynamical.org/catalog/noaa-refs-forecast-hourly-virtual/validation/) for variable availability, missing data, known quirks, fill values, value distributions, and sample plots.
description_model:
The RRFS Ensemble Forecast System (REFS) is a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP) ensemble product system. It produces ensemble products on a 3 km grid, including means, spreads and probabilities of exceeding thresholds, from the current and 6 hour old cycles of the deterministic Rapid Refresh Forecast System (RRFS) and its ensemble (RRFS ENS), plus two HRRR members over the continental United States.

NOAA REFS is pre-operational, so expect changes to the model data and to the structure of this dataset.

variants.label: dynamical-catalog
variants.code:
import dynamical_catalog  # dynamical-catalog>=1.0.1

ds = dynamical_catalog.open("noaa-refs-forecast-hourly-virtual", chunks=None)
ds["temperature_2m"].sel(init_time="2026-09-16T12", lead_time="24h", statistic="mean")

variants.label: pystac
variants.code:
import icechunk
import pystac
import xarray as xr

catalog = pystac.Catalog.from_file("https://stac.dynamical.org/catalog.json")
collection = catalog.get_child("noaa-refs-forecast-hourly-virtual")
asset = collection.assets["icechunk-https"]

authorize = icechunk.containers_credentials({"s3://noaa-rrfs-ops-pds/": icechunk.s3_anonymous_credentials()})
repo = icechunk.Repository.open(
    icechunk.http_storage(asset.href),
    authorize_virtual_chunk_access=authorize,
)
session = repo.readonly_session("main")

ds = xr.open_zarr(session.store, chunks=None)
ds["temperature_2m"].sel(init_time="2026-09-16T12", lead_time="24h", statistic="mean")

fog_liquid_water_content_0m.comment: Fog liquid water is derived by the ensemble generator. Mean is weighted over members with positive fog liquid water. Standard deviation divides the weighted sum of squared deviations from that mean over all nonmissing members, including zero-fog members, by the positive-member weight sum before taking the square root. Both are zero when no member has fog.

geopotential_height_cloud_base.comment: Mean and standard deviation use only members with a cloud base. When none contribute, the mean holds the source's no-cloud value and the standard deviation is zero, which does not indicate measured certainty.

geopotential_height_cloud_ceiling.comment: Mean and standard deviation exclude capped members. A mean of 20000 m denotes no reported cloud ceiling; zero standard deviation can indicate no uncapped members as well as agreement.

geopotential_height_surface.comment: Standard deviation reflects differences in terrain height between member grids.

soil_temperature_0m.comment: Over water, absent member soil values enter the statistics as raw zero before Celsius conversion, while some members may contribute nonzero values. Means and standard deviations there are not soil temperature quantities. These cells are not marked; use a land mask. The standard_deviation slice is not populated; read soil_temperature_0m_standard_deviation without the statistic dimension, in kelvin differences; 1 K of difference equals 1 degree_Celsius of difference.

soil_temperature_0m_standard_deviation.comment: Over water, absent member soil values enter the statistics as raw zero before Celsius conversion, while some members may contribute nonzero values. Means and standard deviations there are not soil temperature quantities. These cells are not marked; use a land mask. NOAA spread: member-weighted population standard deviation with weights normalized over contributing members. This is a temperature difference in K, numerically equal to the difference in degree_Celsius; no temperature offset is applied.

temperature_250hpa.comment: The standard_deviation slice is not populated; read temperature_250hpa_standard_deviation without the statistic dimension, in kelvin differences; 1 K of difference equals 1 degree_Celsius of difference.

temperature_250hpa_standard_deviation.comment: NOAA spread: member-weighted population standard deviation with weights normalized over contributing members. This is a temperature difference in K, numerically equal to the difference in degree_Celsius; no temperature offset is applied.

temperature_2m_standard_deviation.comment: NOAA spread: member-weighted population standard deviation with weights normalized over contributing members. This is a temperature difference in K, numerically equal to the difference in degree_Celsius; no temperature offset is applied.

vertical_velocity_geometric_700_500mb.comment: Vertical velocity in a layer defined by pressure differences above ground, rather than an isobaric layer.

vertical_wind_shear_0_6000m.comment: Mean is the weighted mean of member speeds. Standard deviation is sqrt(var(u) + var(v)), the vector spread including variation in direction, rather than the standard deviation of speed.

vertical_wind_shear_0_609m.comment: Over terrain above roughly 1500 to 1800 m the source does not compute the shear and writes 0. Mean is the weighted mean of member speeds. Standard deviation is sqrt(var(u) + var(v)), the vector spread including variation in direction, rather than the standard deviation of speed.

visibility_surface.comment: Mean and standard deviation exclude members capped at the no-event visibility limit. A large mean can represent the cap when no uncapped member remains; the corresponding zero standard deviation does not imply agreement.

volumetric_soil_moisture_0m.comment: Over water, absent member soil values enter the statistics as zero, while some members may contribute nonzero values. Means and standard deviations there are not soil moisture quantities. These cells are not marked; use a land mask.
